entry.title: Quick Fix: System Number Mismatch in MiniSAP (Developer Trial 2022/2023)
entry.content:
When setting up the ABAP Cloud Developer Trial (MiniSAP)—as referenced in the abap-cloud-developer-trial-2022-available-now—you may encounter an issue when installing your trial license via transaction SLICENSE:, transaction SLICENSE fails with this error:

❌ "This system’s system number is “000000000xxxxxx”, but there is a licence key for system number “000000000yyyyy” in the licence key file."

The Cause

The new license generation page: 🔗 https://zlicensekeyminisap-supportportal.dispatcher.hana.ondemand.com/?hc_reset#/minisap

Generates a file named A4H_Multiple.txt that contains a mismatched SYSTEM-NR parameter which does not match your local system.

Quick Solution

  1. Get your System Number: Open SLICENSE in MiniSAP and note your actual System Number (e.g., 000000000xxxxxx).

  2. Edit A4H_Multiple.txt: Open the license file downloaded from the portal in a text editor (Notepad, VS Code, etc.).

  3. Replace SYSTEM-NR: Find the SYSTEM-NR field—which appears twice in the file—and replace its value with your local System Number.

  4. Install: Save the file and upload it in SLICENSE.

Problem solved! 🚀

@SAP

entry.title: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – J1IG STO BAdI: GR Validation and Reference Number Change Not Work
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

We have a requirement in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition related to the India GST STO process.

Application:

Create Inbound Invoices for STOs – India (J1IG / J_1IG_INV)

We are using:

  • BAdI: BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD

  • Method: CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

  • Custom Implementation: YY1_STO_CLOUD

We have two requirements, but currently neither requirement is working as expected.

Requirement 1 – Block J1IG if GRN is not posted

J1IG should not allow creation/posting of the inbound GST invoice/FI vendor document if the STO PO does not have a valid Goods Receipt.

Expected behavior:

STO PO → GR 101 → J1IG Inbound GST Invoice

If Movement Type 101 has not been posted, J1IG should stop the process with an error.

Also, if 101 was posted and completely reversed by 102, it should not be considered a valid GR.

We attempted to implement this validation in:

BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD → CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

However, J1IG is still proceeding even when the required GR has not been posted.

Requirement 2 – Change J1IG Reference Number

Currently, when we click Create Inbound GST Invoice in J1IG, the Reference Number is automatically populated with the ODN / GST Sequence Number.

Current:

Reference Number = ODN / GST Sequence Number

Required:

Reference Number = STO Outbound Billing Document Number

The required billing document is the STO Billing – GST Out. Inv. document.

We attempted to change this using:

BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD → CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

However, the ODN number is still being populated and the STO billing document number is not appearing.

Our question

Could an SAP expert please advise:

  1. Is BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD / CHANGE_BEFORE_POST the correct BAdI to implement both requirements?

  2. How can we check for a valid 101 GR not completely reversed by 102 in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?

  3. How can we stop J1IG posting from this BAdI when GR is missing?

  4. Which exact field/structure controls the J1IG Reference Number?

  5. Is there another released BAdI/API required to replace the ODN with the STO billing document number?

  6. Is the Reference Number overwritten by standard J1IG processing after CHANGE_BEFORE_POST?

We are looking for a released/clean-core solution for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

We can provide our current YY1_STO_CLOUD implementation and screenshots if required.

Thank you.

entry.title: Discrepancy between SM12 output and ENQUEUE_READ RFM
entry.content:
Hi,

We executed SM12 without any selection filters and observed approximately 7,261 lock entries. We then executed the ENQUEUE_READ RFM without selection filters and received approximately 13,714 records.

We would like to understand the reason for this discrepancy. In particular, we have observed that the timestamps for apparently corresponding entries are not identical—for example, an entry appears around 03:10 in SM12, whereas the corresponding information returned by ENQUEUE_READ appears around 03:14.

Could you please clarify the following:

  1. Does SM12 apply any grouping, aggregation, or consolidation when displaying lock entries? If so, which fields are used as the grouping criteria?
  2. Does ENQUEUE_READ return a different granularity of lock information compared with what SM12 displays—for example, multiple owner/lock entries associated with the same lock argument
  3. What is the recommended way to obtain a result from ENQUEUE_READ that is directly comparable with the lock count displayed by SM12?
  4. If SM12 and ENQUEUE_READ are expected to represent different levels of the enqueue lock table, please clarify the relationship between lock owner, lock argument, and elementary lock/lock entry, and which of these is counted by SM12 versus returned by ENQUEUE_READ.

Thanks

entry.title: Fiori Elements OData V2: Incorrect object-page header and navigation hierarchy in a nested RAP BO
entry.content:
I am developing a custom transactional application using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The application uses managed RAP business objects, CDS view entities, projection views, behavior definitions, and a Fiori Elements UI exposed through an OData V2 UI service.

My business object has the following composition hierarchy:

  • Customer — root entity

  • Customer Role — child of Customer

  • Customer Address — child of Customer

  • Company Code — child of Customer

  • Tax — child of Company Code

The entities have technical UUID keys, and the child entities are connected through RAP compositions and parent associations.

Issue

The application displays object pages, but the navigation hierarchy and object-page header are not behaving as expected.

For example, on the Customer Address object page, the header displays a slash-separated value resembling:

8001 /

On the Tax object page, the header displays:

8001 / /

The navigation/header behavior appears inconsistent across the composition hierarchy. I want to understand whether this is caused by the RAP composition and association definitions, CDS annotations, or the way Fiori Elements resolves object-page navigation context.

Questions

  1. How does Fiori Elements determine the slash-separated header and navigation context for nested RAP composition entities?

  2. What could cause the object-page header or navigation hierarchy to display incomplete or unexpected values?

  3. Which RAP composition, parent-association, projection, or UI annotation settings should be checked to ensure navigation works correctly across multiple composition levels?

entry.title: Alternative Approach for Mass Upload of Recurring Journal Entry Templates in SAP S/4HANA Public Clou

Hello Experts,

I am looking for guidance on a requirement in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud related to the creation of recurring journal entries at scale.

Business Requirement

We need to mass create/upload a large number of recurring journal entry templates in the system. The objective is to avoid manual creation of each recurring journal entry through the Fiori application Manage Recurring Journal Entries app (F1598)  due to the high volume involved.

After reviewing the available standard applications and APIs, we have encountered the following limitations:

  1. The Manage Recurring Journal Entries Fiori application does not appear to provide any standard Excel upload / mass upload capability for creating recurring journal entries.

  2. The application is based on the OData service/API: FAC_RECURRING_ACCOUNTING_DOC_SRV However, this service appears to be an unreleased API and therefore cannot be consumed for custom development or integrations in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, where only released APIs are supported.


Could the community please suggest a supported approach in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud for:

A. Mass creation of recurring journal entries

B. Mass upload of recurring journal entry templates

C. Available released APIs, migration objects, or public-cloud-compliant integration options

D. Recommended best practices followed by other customers facing similar requirements

Thank you in advance for your support.

entry.title: SAP PP/ABAP: Recursive BOM Explosion for Cross-Plant Special Procurement Items
entry.content:
Requirement

I have a requirement to develop a program that can explode a BOM (Bill of Material) containing items with a Special Procurement Key at the item level.

Currently, these items are not being exploded further because of cross-plant references, either through CS11 or the standard BOM explosion BAPI.

My Approach / Proposed Solution

I am planning to develop a custom program using a recursive approach.

1. I have created a method that performs BOM explosion for a single BOM input. The method explodes the BOM and stores all the child items in a global internal table within the class.

2. During the explosion, whenever an item with a Special Procurement Key is encountered, the program retrieves the relevant plant, alternative BOM, and BOM usage details from the MAST and T406 tables.

3. Using these details, the program triggers the BOM explosion for the corresponding BOM in the other plant.

4. This process continues recursively until no further items with a Special Procurement Key are found at any level of the BOM hierarchy.

5. Finally, all the exploded components are stored in the global internal table.

What do you think about this approach?

Is this approach technically feasible in SAP ABAP? Are there any standard SAP function modules, BAPIs, or better alternatives to handle cross-plant BOM explosion scenarios?

I would appreciate your suggestions and recommendations on potential challenges, performance optimization, or best practices for implementing this solution.
